implementationPlan.description: Create a dedicated composition suite and add the first cross-feature integration test around the real `submitPlanTool`/StateManager path. First assert that submitting the missing path without `newFiles` rejects with the teaching error naming the path and the `newFiles` remedy while leaving the task unmodified. Then resubmit the same multi-step plan with the missing path declared in `newFiles`, and assert the persisted plan retains `newFiles`, the absent explicit budget is seeded as `stepCount * pacePerStepMs`, and the size warning is persisted/returned. Exact assertions must ensure removing any one of the budget, path, or size gates breaks the test, while existing files pass unchanged and the test performs all filesystem setup/cleanup within its temporary project.

implementationPlan.description: In the same suite, add the second cross-feature integration test for one release/human-unpark/claim flow using the real `releaseTaskTool` and `claimNextTaskTool`. Freeze time; seed two recent qualifying empty-progress handoffs; mock only the disk-signature boundary to return a release signature and then a different claim signature; perform the third assigned-worker empty-progress release and assert it persists the newest handoff/disk signature, idles the prior worker, returns `cascadeTriggered`, and parks the task in BACKLOG with the explanatory governor message. Simulate the documented human re-enable by moving the now-unassigned task back to WORKING, claim it with a new worker, and assert the response reports `staleHandoffDiskState: true` plus a re-verification hint while retaining the handoff history. Include error handling assertions that chat notification failure cannot undo the park and an undefined recomputation produces no false stale flag, without invoking a real git binary or leaving timers/mocks behind.

implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial review of the whole epic diff (git diff f785be3 → working tree: 45 files, +3341/-733), not just my own tasks.

CONCURRENCY: no git subprocess runs under the state mutex on either side — releaseTask computes the signature pre-mutex with the shape validation, claimNextTask stashes the stored value inside runExclusive and recomputes only after it returns, both documented at the call site. diskState.ts uses execFile with an args array (never a shell string), 3s timeout, 8MB maxBuffer, windowsHide; `git` is git.exe so the Windows .cmd-shim trap does not apply. submit_plan keeps rails → size → async path probe → ONE updateTask, so a rejection cannot half-write; complete_task runs the branch check with the other assertions BEFORE updateTask for the same reason. Every new chat post is individually try/caught. chat_wait was NOT reviewed — task-aa44c1be was qa_rejected (reopenCount 1) and its bytes are being rewritten by worker-f5977052 right now; reviewing a moving target would be theatre, and its subscribe-before-drain/cursor claims belong to that task's own QA pass.

NULL/EMPTY + DEFAULT-VS-EXPLICIT-FALSE: claimNextTask reads appendOnlyFiles with `??`, never `||`, so an explicit `[]` still disables suppression; refusalCascadeAutoBacklog is read as `!== false` so absence stays enabled; consolidationBranch type-guards a hand-edited non-string into "disabled" rather than throwing; matchesBranchPattern returns false (never throws) for non-strings, empty values, >255-char branches and uncompilable patterns; compileAppendOnlyMatchers guards a non-array setting (a string would compile one matcher per character) and skips non-string/over-long entries; findMissingPaths fails open on anything but ENOENT/ENOTDIR; computeDiskStateSignature returns undefined on every failure and callers treat undefined as "unknown", never "unchanged".

SANITIZER PERSISTENCE: sanitizeImplementationPlan carries every new step field — newFiles (sibling) and amendments/activeAmendmentId (mine) — and both have tests asserting through state.getTask rather than the object handed to updateTask.

REGISTRATION / ROLE GATES / COUNTERS: moe.amend_plan_step is in getTools(); its architect-or-governor gate fails closed on a missing workerId, mirroring submit_plan_critique. No QA counter was repurposed — reopenCount/reopenReason are untouched by the refusal cascade (the archived branch mutated them; deliberately not carried forward), and nextStatusForRelease is unchanged, with the cascade reusing its existing 'park' context.

TEACHING ERRORS: the missing-path error names the offending paths, the project root, and both concrete fixes; the size-gate error names counts, thresholds and moe.create_task; BRANCH-POLICY-FAIL names both branches and the recovery; the amendment rejections point at moe.request_replan. No forbidden pattern (eval(, innerHTML, dangerouslySetInnerHTML, __proto__) appears in the diff.

FINDING + NARROW FIX (concurrency/hardening): the epic shipped TWO glob compilers and only one was hardened. util/branchPolicy.ts caps wildcards and collapses adjacent `.*`; util/affectedFiles.ts expanded every `**/` to a fresh `(?:[^/]+/)*`, so a pattern like '**/'.repeat(50) chained 50 ambiguous stars — and computeFileCollisions runs INSIDE claim_next_task under runExclusive, where a hang freezes tool dispatch fleet-wide. Previously recorded as accepted-not-blocking, but the gate task is where it gets fixed. Fix: collapse adjacent expansions (skip the group when source already ends with it, same for `.*`), semantics identical. Added a test asserting `**/**/notes.md` still matches at depth and at zero depth, still rejects a non-match, and that the pathological pattern completes in <1s. Mutation-proved: reverting the collapse makes that single case take 102.7 SECONDS of backtracking; with it the whole file runs in under a second.

DOCS: covered in step-5 — one real omission found and fixed (appendOnlyFiles was absent from all of docs/MCP_SERVER.md, so the claim_next_task fileCollision contract never mentioned the suppression).

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Adding assertions to one sibling's focused suite was rejected because each requested flow spans multiple tools/settings and needs an explicit composition boundary; a dedicated `governancePlaneV2.integration.test.ts` keeps the epic gate discoverable and avoids diluting mutation-resistant sibling tests. Using a real temporary git repository for the release/claim composition was rejected: `diskState.test.ts` already owns subprocess/parser coverage, while this test should deterministically prove the release and claim consumers compose by mocking only the signature boundary. Reimplementing missing sibling behavior in the final task was rejected because the epic is actively landing in a shared tree; the gate must detect integration defects, not create duplicate competing implementations. A documentation snapshot test was rejected as brittle; the required three-file semantic sweep plus full suite/root lint is the narrower production check.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: The epic base before feature work is filing commit `f785be3`, so the final adversarial review can compare the complete current diff against that point. `submit_plan` now composes existing plan-size enforcement with sibling budget/path changes, and its test must prove rejection leaves the task unchanged before a corrected resubmit exercises all successful outputs. Disk-state capture and refusal counting both extend `releaseTask.ts`, while stale-state comparison decorates `claimNextTask.ts`; a single release→human re-enable→claim test is the highest-value merge-conflict detector. The full daemon suite is the task's named evidence gate; root `npm run lint` is separately required by the DoD and needs Git Bash on Windows. The existing release/claim chat posts are best-effort and current tests use temporary StateManager fixtures, so the integration suite can stay daemon-free and deterministic.
planningNotes.risks: The final task may be claimed before lower-order siblings have actually landed; treating absent features as code to recreate would cause shared-tree collisions, so the preflight must fail closed on sequencing. Vitest module mocks can leak across files if not restored; the dedicated suite must use hoisted mocks deliberately and reset timers/mocks in cleanup. The release test must simulate the human BACKLOG→WORKING gate explicitly—claiming BACKLOG directly would test an illegal lifecycle. A passing happy-path submit alone would not prove the missing-path gate, so the same test needs the initial rejection and corrected resubmit. Documentation is most vulnerable to stale claims about release parking, chat cursor behavior, amendment persistence, and missing-currentBranch handling. Global rails require literal error handling/test coverage and prohibit the listed unsafe patterns in plan/code text.
